title: Prospect and qualify
lead: Sales OR Business Developer; Account Manager involved throughout.
trigger: A potentially suitable business or an inbound lead is identified.
inputs: Social-channel review, contact details and a relevant service need; lead source.
steps: Use on-ground visits, researched cold calls, LinkedIn search, email campaigns or calls to leads generated by PMP media buying.
Record the opportunity, contact, need, outreach outcome and next action in the agreed lead register. The lead-register tool and fields are proposed pending owner confirmation.
Book an online or offline first meeting. Keep the Account Manager involved.
Prepare a prospect/client-named folder inside PMP Drive / Quotations. Sales or BD is accountable for folder setup.
output: Qualified opportunity, first meeting booked and pre-contract folder.
gate: Do not confuse a booked meeting with a signed client or permission to start contracted delivery.
record: Lead/contact record and meeting details; prospect folder reference.

title: Prepare the audit and initial proposal
lead: Sales/BD prepares and studies the meeting material; Account Manager involved.
inputs: Available business brief, social URLs, website, asset access and current/historical pricing evidence.
steps: Use supplied SKILL-1.md (SSM Strategy): confirm scope, format, language and available access.
Research before prescribing: brief, social channels, website, assets, competitors and category context. Record dated sources and what cannot be verified.
Label Observed facts, Interpretation and Recommendation separately. Public views alone do not prove paid boosting.
Prepare an initial strategy/proposal and three quotation tiers after the audit. Use actual market ranges, previous PMP prices, client industry/class and proposed scope.
Study the actual problems and proposed solutions carefully before meeting one.
output: Evidence-based audit, initial proposal strategy and three suggested quotation tiers.
gate: The strategy skill supplies a research method, not an agency rate card or quotation formula. No invented prices or audit facts.
record: Audit/proposal deck, research notes, source dates, pricing references and declared gaps.

title: First meeting and readiness to sign
trigger: Prepared first meeting takes place online or offline.
inputs: Audit, initial strategy, three quotation tiers and client questions.
steps: Present observed problems, proposed solutions and scope options.
Capture the actual client brief: objectives, priorities, constraints, service needs and information that differs from the initial assumptions.
Establish whether the client is ready to sign the contract. Record that readiness separately from actual signature.
If not ready, keep the opportunity in pre-sales follow-up; actual-strategy development remains pending.
output: Actual meeting brief and an explicit client-readiness status.
gate: Meeting one alone does not authorize actual-strategy development. Client readiness to sign is required.
record: Meeting notes, actual brief, readiness record and next action.

title: Develop the actual strategy
lead: Account Manager with Social Media Specialist, Marketing Manager and Media Buyer.
trigger: Meeting one completed AND client confirms readiness to sign.
inputs: Sales/BD skill-generated pre-meeting strategy plus actual client brief captured from the meeting.
steps: AM compares the initial proposal with the actual brief and identifies mismatches, new requirements and assumptions needing correction.
AM develops the actual strategy with Social Media Specialist, Marketing Manager and Media Buyer.
Apply the supplied strategy method to the agreed scope; revisit evidence and disclose gaps rather than carrying unsupported proposal assumptions forward.
Reconcile strategy-driven scope changes with the agreed quotation before printing the second-meeting pack.
output: Actual client-brief-based strategy and aligned scope/quotation.
gate: This is readiness-gated pre-contract strategy preparation. It is distinct from contracted production, which remains subject to signing and payment.
record: Actual strategy, current brief, scope changes and quotation version.

title: Second meeting, signatures and folder move
lead: Sales/BD prepares the pack; Account Manager remains involved.
trigger: Client ready to sign; actual strategy and agreed scope/quotation prepared.
inputs: Printed client brief, actual strategy, agreed quotation and contract.
steps: Present all four printed materials at meeting two.
Client signs the client brief, actual strategy, agreed quotation and contract.
On contract signing, Sales or BD moves the SAME folder from PMP Drive / Quotations / [Client name] to PMP Drive / [Client name]. Do not duplicate it.
Retain quotation records and organize Start Strategy, Client Brief, Content/monthly calendars, Design/monthly final designs, Videos/monthly final videos and other scope-specific work.
AM opens the project WhatsApp group with client, PMP owner, Marketing Manager and relevant stakeholders.
output: Signed commercial pack, standalone client folder and kickoff communication group.
gate: Signature triggers folder movement. It does not by itself authorize contracted delivery.
record: Signed materials, moved folder reference and group membership.

title: Confirm payment before contracted delivery
lead: Sales/BD and AM coordinate the handover; payment-verification authority must be confirmed by the owner.
inputs: Agreed contract service category, contract amount and verified payment evidence.
steps: For SOCIAL MEDIA MANAGEMENT ONLY: require 100% of the agreed contract amount before contracted work starts.
For a contract INCLUDING OTHER SERVICES: require at least 50% of the agreed contract amount before contracted work starts.
Record payment evidence and confirmation from the authorized verifier. A verbal claim or demo calculator is not verification of funds.
Treat the media-buying fee separately: after executing the plan, calculate the user-described 25% retainer on verified ACTUAL media expenses.
output: Recorded delivery-readiness decision with payment evidence.
gate: Signed pack plus required upfront payment gates contracted delivery. Remaining balance timing, taxes, media-spend funding and billable expense definition follow the agreement and remain unconfirmed here.
record: Payment confirmation, agreed category, contract reference and later actual-media-spend evidence.

title: Brief, assign and monitor production
lead: Account Manager coordinates; heads and accountable task holders execute.
trigger: Signed pack and required upfront payment confirmed.
inputs: Actual strategy, approved scope, client brief and available assets.
steps: AM writes the actionable production brief and distributes tasks to Content, Design and Editing.
Give every task one accountable holder. Include account, priority, deadline, task brief, inputs, output/reference and required reviewer.
Record start/end dates as work progresses and keep task links, reviewer notes and task-holder notes current.
AM monitors execution, follows up on blockers and keeps the client context connected to the work.
Where a task has multiple contributors, identify one accountable owner; do not silently treat a shared sheet entry as ownership by everyone.
output: Trackable tasks and a current execution view.
gate: Required assets and upstream work must be available before a handoff. Exact SLAs, escalation thresholds and reassignment authority need owner confirmation.

title: Submit work and execute comments
lead: Task holder submits; AM, Marketing Manager and relevant head provide comments.
trigger: Assigned output is ready for review or a reviewer requests changes.
inputs: Task record, output, brief reference and review comments.
steps: Content submits work on the sheet and uploads the working calendar PPTX to Content / relevant month; comments and revisions remain on that SAME calendar PPTX.
Design and Video submit work for review and update task-sheet references. The draft-review location is not specified; do not invent a mandatory Drive draft folder.
AM, Marketing Manager and relevant heads write actionable comments. Record author and context, not just a generic rejected status.
The task remains open until its accountable holder executes every comment and records the response.
Resubmit corrected work for review; do not assume a previous approval still covers revised material.
output: Reviewable work, resolved-comment responses and a revision history.
gate: An unresolved comment keeps the task open. A daily-finished entry or completed edit is not proof of approval.
record: Task notes, holder notes, same Content calendar and revised output references.

title: Quality and final internal approval
lead: Content head / Design head for their teams; Marketing Manager for video quality AND final internal approval.
inputs: Current task output, actual brief and review history.
steps: Content work: Head of Content reviews quality, then Marketing Manager approves.
Design work: Head of Design reviews quality, then Marketing Manager approves.
Video work: Marketing Manager performs video-quality review and final internal approval. Editors report directly to Marketing Manager.
Record the quality-review result and Marketing approval as distinct decisions even when the same Marketing Manager performs both video checks.
If any reviewer rejects the task, return it to its holder with comments and repeat the required review after correction.
output: Internally finalized tasks eligible for AM collection.
gate: Internal quality approval, Marketing approval and final client approval are different milestones. Owner receipt of this SOP does not automatically transfer all MM authority.
record: Reviewer, decision, date, output version/reference and comments.

title: Collect one presentation and obtain client approval
lead: Account Manager; client provides final external approval.
trigger: All included work has passed quality review and Marketing approval.
inputs: Finalized Content, Design and Video outputs and current calendar.
steps: AM gathers the finalized deliverables into ONE client PPTX and checks that it matches the approved brief and scope.
AM presents that PPTX to the client and records the client’s final approval for the presented version.
If the client rejects or requests changes, AM logs the comments, routes affected tasks back to their holders and monitors correction.
Repeat applicable internal reviews and collect the corrected presentation for renewed client approval.
After internal and client approval, archive final Design and Video copies in the correct monthly folders. Content calendars retain their working-review role.
output: Client-approved presentation and approved final archive references.
gate: No publication before final client approval. Keep the approval tied to the actual presented version; do not reuse approval for changed material.
record: Presentation reference/version, final client approval evidence and archived final links.

title: Schedule, publish and manage the community
lead: Social Media Specialist; Media Buyer remains a separate paid-execution role.
trigger: AM hands over the client-approved presentation/calendar.
inputs: Approved content, final asset links, agreed schedule and platform access.
steps: Social Media Specialist gathers private-label calendars and consolidates scheduling requirements.
Schedule and publish the approved calendars; retain publication references.
Reply to comments on private-label pages. Maintain the account’s agreed voice and route issues outside approved responses to AM/MM. Exact response-time targets are not yet confirmed.
Keep organic publication separate from paid activation. Paid work requires its agreed media plan, authorizations and funding; exact financial approval ownership must be confirmed.
If material changes after approval, return through the relevant review chain before publication.
output: Scheduled/published work, community responses and live references.
gate: An internal final-approval label alone is not external client approval. The demo website does not publish, send messages or enforce real permissions.
record: Publishing calendar, live links, response records and exception log.

title: Report, optimise and inform scale
lead: Social Media Specialist and Media Buyer, coordinated by AM and Marketing Manager.
trigger: Activity is live and performance/listening evidence becomes available.
inputs: Published work, available platform data, actual paid-media spend and client objectives.
steps: Social Media Specialist creates performance reports, listening reports and social strategy updates, in addition to calendar and community duties.
Media Buyer provides paid performance and verified actual media expenses; calculate the 25% post-execution fee from the agreed actual-expense basis.
AM gathers the client-facing reporting narrative; MM reviews strategic implications and next actions.
Feed findings into Diagnose, Design and Optimise. Scale only on supporting evidence and agreed scope; do not promise growth, ROAS or other results without evidence.
Record data gaps, recommendations and decisions. Weekly/monthly reporting appears in the supplied strategy framework; account-specific deadlines must be agreed.
output: Performance/listening reports, actual-spend evidence, optimisation actions and proposed next-cycle plan.
gate: No fabricated metrics, benchmarks, savings or revenue impact. Confirm reporting cadence and financial basis before operational adoption.
record: Reports, source dates, actual-spend records and action log.
